title: Hyperkalemia with Peaked T-Waves
priorityInterventions: IV Calcium Gluconate (1-2 g) immediately to stabilize cardiac cell membranes
IV Regular Insulin 10 units + D50 50 mL push + Inhaled Albuterol to shift K+ into cells
Furosemide / Lokelma / emergent hemodialysis to eliminate potassium
Continuous 12-lead monitoring to anticipate QRS widening into sine-wave arrest

title: Unstable Monomorphic Ventricular Tachycardia
priorityInterventions: Check pulse immediately (differentiate pulseless VT vs VT with pulse)
If pulse present but unstable (hypotension, altered mental status): Immediate Synchronized Cardioversion at 100 J biphasic
Place defibrillator/pacing combo pads on patient (anterior-posterior or sternum-apex)
If pulseless: Call code blue, start CPR, immediate unsynchronized defibrillation (120-200 J)

title: Second-Degree AV Block Mobitz Type II
priorityInterventions: Attach transcutaneous pacing pads immediately (high risk of sudden complete heart block)
Avoid AV nodal blockers (beta-blockers, CCBs, digoxin)
Prepare Atropine 1 mg push (note: often ineffective in infranodal Mobitz II)
Notify cardiology and prepare for temporary transvenous pacing

title: Critical Drug-Induced QTc Prolongation
priorityInterventions: Immediately hold all QT-prolonging drugs (Ondansetron, Haloperidol, Amiodarone, Azithromycin)
Check serum potassium and magnesium levels (target K+ > 4.0 mEq/L, Mg2+ > 2.0 mg/dL)
Administer IV Magnesium Sulfate (1-2 g over 15-60 min; rapid push if Torsades ensues)
Continuous cardiac monitoring with defibrillator at bedside

title: Acute Inferior STEMI
priorityInterventions: Activate cardiac catheterization team immediately (target door-to-balloon < 90 min)
Chewable Aspirin 325 mg immediately
Obtain right-sided ECG (V4R) before giving Nitroglycerin (rule out RV infarction)
Apply defibrillator pads and secure dual large-bore IV lines

title: Elderly Syncope with Bradycardic AFib & Left Bundle Branch Block / STEMI-Equivalent
prompt: I have a 80 year-old female patient presented in the ED with syncope and having falls. The ECG shows heart rate of about 45 beats per minute. The QRS complexes are irregular and are 150ms. There are no clear P waves. There are ST-Elevation and negative QRS to V1, V2, and V3. V6 has a positive QRS complex.
priorityInterventions: Apply transcutaneous combo pacing pads immediately to stabilize severe bradycardia (45 bpm)
Establish dual large-bore IV access and cycle vitals every 2-3 minutes
Strict bed rest and fall precautions for post-syncope elderly patient
Stat 12-lead ECG and chart review to compare prior ECG (evaluate modified Sgarbossa criteria / new LBBB anterior STEMI-equivalent)
Withhold all AV nodal blocking medications (beta-blockers, CCBs, digoxin)
Prepare for emergent transvenous or permanent pacemaker (PPM) placement and cath lab activation if Sgarbossa positive
